records.gloss: For the director, Do not destroy, of David, a miktam.
pieces: For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A miktam.

L.1: For the director: "Do not destroy." Of David. A miktam.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: Do not destroy: probably the name of a tune
alternatives: a plea set at the head of the psalm
decisions.reason: The words ('al tashchet) also head Psalms 57, 59 and 75. They may name a melody the psalm was sung to. Moses prays the same words in Deuteronomy 9:26.

decisions.choice: miktam: a kind of psalm whose meaning is unknown
decisions.reason: As in 16:1. The word heads Psalms 16 and 56-60; its meaning is lost.

decisions.choice: To the tune
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the words are probably the name of a tune (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: A song
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown, so Readable says only that it is a song.

records.heading: A God who judges the earth

records.source: הַֽאֻמְנָ֗ם אֵ֣לֶם צֶ֭דֶק תְּדַבֵּר֑וּן מֵישָׁרִ֥ים תִּ֝שְׁפְּט֗וּ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Indeed, gods, righteousness do you speak? With uprightness do you judge [the] children of humankind?
pieces: You gods, do you really speak what is right? \q Do you judge human beings fairly?

L.2: Do you indeed speak righteousness, [you] gods? \q Do you judge the children of humankind with uprightness?

R.2: You rulers who act like gods, do you really say what is right? \q Do you judge people fairly?

decisions.choice: gods: the mighty ones who rule
alternatives: in silence (as the word is pointed): do you indeed speak righteousness in silence?
decisions.reason: The consonants of this word, as the vowels in the Hebrew text point them, mean "silence", which gives little sense. With other vowels they mean "gods" or "mighty ones", which fits the parallel "children of humankind" and the rulers called "gods" in Psalm 82:1, 6. The word is read that way here.

decisions.choice: the children of humankind: those who are judged
decisions.reason: The words are most naturally the object: do these rulers judge people fairly? They could also be a second address, "you human beings".

decisions.choice: a question expecting "no"
decisions.reason: The question is an accusation. Verse 3 gives the answer: they plan injustice.

decisions.choice: You rulers who act like gods
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant (m1).

records.source: אַף־בְּלֵב֮ עוֹלֹ֪ת תִּפְעָ֫ל֥וּן בָּאָ֡רֶץ חֲמַ֥ס יְ֝דֵיכֶ֗ם תְּפַלֵּֽסֽוּן׃
records.gloss: No, in heart injustices you do; on the earth [the] violence of your hands you weigh out.
pieces: No, in your hearts you plan wrong, \q and on earth your hands deal out violence by weight.

L.3: No, in [your] heart you work injustices; \q on the earth you weigh out the violence of your hands.

R.3: No! In your hearts you plan evil. \q Then you hand out violence on the earth, as if you were weighing it on scales.

decisions.choice: weigh out: deal out as a judge
decisions.reason: Weighing is the work of fair trade and fair judging (Proverbs 16:11). These judges weigh out violence instead of justice.

decisions.choice: injustices: wrongs done in judging
decisions.reason: The word ('avlah) is the opposite of justice; it is what an unjust judge does.

decisions.choice: as if you were weighing it on scales
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: זֹ֣רוּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים מֵרָ֑חֶם תָּע֥וּ מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן דֹּבְרֵ֥י כָזָֽב׃
records.gloss: They are estranged, [the] wicked, from [the] womb; they go astray from [the] belly, speakers of a lie.
pieces: From the womb the wicked have turned aside; \q from birth those who tell lies have wandered off.

L.4: The wicked are estranged from the womb; \q they go astray from the belly, speakers of a lie.

R.4: Wicked people go the wrong way from the day they are born. \q From birth they wander off and tell lies.

decisions.choice: from the womb, from the belly: from birth
decisions.reason: The words describe people whose whole lives have gone wrong; compare 51:7.

decisions.choice: are estranged: have turned away
decisions.reason: The verb (zur) is used of turning away and becoming a stranger.

records.source: חֲמַת־לָ֗מוֹ כִּדְמ֥וּת חֲמַת־נָחָ֑שׁ כְּמוֹ־פֶ֥תֶן חֵ֝רֵ֗שׁ יַאְטֵ֥ם אָזְנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Venom [is] to them like [the] likeness of venom of a snake, like a cobra deaf [that] shuts its ear,
pieces: Their poison is like a snake's poison, \q like a cobra that is deaf and stops up its ear,

L.5: Venom [is] theirs, like the venom of a snake, \q like a deaf cobra [that] shuts its ear,

R.5: What they say is like poison from a snake. \q They are like a cobra that will not listen and closes its ears.

decisions.choice: cobra: a poisonous snake
decisions.reason: The word (peten) names a deadly snake (Deuteronomy 32:33); "cobra" is a likely identification.

decisions.choice: a deaf cobra: a snake no charmer can control
decisions.reason: Snake charmers were known in the ancient Near East (Ecclesiastes 10:11; Jeremiah 8:17). A snake that will not hear the charmer cannot be tamed; so with the wicked.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 6, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: What they say
decisions.reason: Readable names the poison as their speech, as verse 4 ends with their lies.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־יִ֭שְׁמַע לְק֣וֹל מְלַחֲשִׁ֑ים חוֹבֵ֖ר חֲבָרִ֣ים מְחֻכָּֽם׃
records.gloss: which not it listens to [the] voice of charmers, of one casting spells skilled.
pieces: so that it does not hear the voice of the charmers, \q however skilled the one who weaves the spell.

L.6: which does not listen to the voice of charmers, \q [nor of] one skilled at casting spells.

R.6: It does not hear the snake charmer, \q even a very skilled one.

decisions.choice: charmers, spells: snake charmers
decisions.reason: The words describe those who charmed snakes with whispered words or music. The psalm uses them only as a picture.

records.source: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים הֲרָס־שִׁנֵּ֥ימוֹ בְּפִ֑ימוֹ מַלְתְּע֥וֹת כְּ֝פִירִ֗ים נְתֹ֣ץ׀יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: God, break their teeth in their mouth; [the] fangs of young lions break off, YHWH.
pieces: God, smash the teeth in their mouths; \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, rip out the young lions' fangs!

L.7: God, break their teeth in their mouth; \q break off the fangs of the young lions, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: God, knock out their teeth! \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, pull out the teeth of these lions so they cannot bite!

decisions.choice: young lions: the wicked as beasts of prey
decisions.reason: The psalm moves from snakes to lions: the unjust rulers devour people. Breaking their teeth means taking away their power to harm (3:8).

decisions.choice: God and the LORD
decisions.reason: Psalms 42-83 mostly call God 'Elohim, "God", where other psalms use the name YHWH. Here both stand side by side; each is rendered as it is in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: so they cannot bite
decisions.reason: Readable says what breaking the teeth means (m1).

records.source: יִמָּאֲס֣וּ כְמוֹ־מַ֭יִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ־לָ֑מוֹ יִדְרֹ֥ךְ חִ֝צָּ֗יו כְּמ֣וֹ יִתְמֹלָֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Let them flow away like water [that] goes about for themselves; [when] he bends his arrows, like [they were] cut off.
pieces: Let them drain away like water running off; \q when they take aim with their arrows, let the shafts be snapped.

L.8: Let them melt away like water [that] runs off; \q [when] he bends his arrows, [let them be] as if cut off.

R.8: Let them disappear like water poured out on the ground. \q When they shoot, let their arrows break.

decisions.choice: his arrows: the word as read
decisions.reason: The word follows the form the Hebrew text's notes say to read; the written form differs slightly. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: he bends his arrows: the wicked takes aim
alternatives: God aims his arrows, and they (the wicked) are cut down
decisions.reason: The line is very short and hard. "He" is most likely each wicked person drawing his bow; the wish is that the arrows fail. It could also be God aiming at them, as in 7:13-14.

decisions.choice: as if cut off: blunted, without points
decisions.reason: The verb (malal) means to be cut off or to wither.

decisions.choice: they ... their
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the wicked as one person here (m2); Balanced and Readable keep the plural of the rest of the verse.

records.source: כְּמ֣וֹ שַׁ֭בְּלוּל תֶּ֣מֶס יַהֲלֹ֑ךְ נֵ֥פֶל אֵ֝֗שֶׁת בַּל־חָ֥זוּ שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: Like a snail [that] melting goes, a miscarriage of a woman — not they have seen [the] sun.
pieces: May they be like a snail that turns to slime as it moves, \q like a baby born dead, who has not looked on the sun.

L.9: Like a snail [that] goes [along] melting away, \q [like] the stillbirth of a woman, [let] them not see the sun.

R.9: May they be like a slug that melts away as it crawls. \q May they be like a baby born dead, who never sees daylight.

decisions.choice: a snail that melts: a slug leaving its trail
decisions.reason: The ancients thought a snail wasted away as it left its slimy trail. The word (temes) is unclear; it may mean melting or slime.

decisions.choice: not they have seen the sun: a wish
decisions.reason: The verb is a statement about the stillborn child, who never sees daylight; set after the wishes of verse 8 it wishes the same for the wicked.

records.source: בְּטֶ֤רֶם יָבִ֣ינוּ סִּֽירֹתֵיכֶ֣ם אָטָ֑ד כְּמוֹ־חַ֥י כְּמוֹ־חָ֝ר֗וֹן יִשְׂעָרֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Before your pots perceive [the] thorn, whether living, whether burning, he will sweep it away.
pieces: Sooner than your pots can sense the thorn fire, \q green or blazing, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sweep it all away in a storm.

L.10: Before your pots perceive the thorn, \q whether green or burning, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sweep it away.

R.10: Before a cooking pot even feels the heat of a fire of thorns, \q God will sweep the wicked away like a storm, \q whether the wood is green or burning.

decisions.choice: before the pots feel the thorns: sudden judgment
alternatives: the thorns themselves (the wicked) are swept away before they can heat the pot
decisions.reason: This is one of the hardest verses in the Psalms. The picture seems to be a fire of thorns under a pot: before it has time to heat, a storm wind sweeps it away. So the end of the wicked will come suddenly. "He" is most likely God.

decisions.choice: living, burning: green or already alight
decisions.reason: "Living" may mean green wood, or raw meat in the pot; "burning" is wood alight or anger.

decisions.choice: sweep away: as with a storm wind
decisions.reason: The verb (sa'ar) is related to the word for a storm (55:9).

decisions.choice: God will sweep the wicked away
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts and who is swept away (m1).

records.source: יִשְׂמַ֣ח צַ֭דִּיק כִּי־חָזָ֣ה נָקָ֑ם פְּעָמָ֥יו יִ֝רְחַ֗ץ בְּדַ֣ם הָרָשָֽׁע׃
records.gloss: He will rejoice, [the] righteous, when he has seen vengeance; his feet he will bathe in [the] blood of the wicked.
pieces: The righteous will be glad when they see justice repaid; \q they will bathe their feet in the wicked's blood.

L.11: The righteous will rejoice when he sees vengeance; \q he will bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked.

R.11: People who do what is right will be glad when they see God punish evil. \q It will be like walking through the blood of the wicked after a battle.

decisions.choice: vengeance: wrongs repaid by God
decisions.reason: The word (naqam) is the punishment God gives to set right what the wicked have done (94:1). The righteous do not take it; they see it.

decisions.choice: bathe his feet in blood: complete victory
decisions.reason: The picture comes from a battlefield after a victory, as in 68:24. It is a strong way of saying that the wicked will be utterly defeated.

decisions.choice: the righteous ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of "the righteous" as one person who stands for all. Balanced and Readable make it plural, which includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: like walking through the blood ... after a battle
alternatives: bathe their feet in the blood
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

records.source: וְיֹאמַ֣ר אָ֭דָם אַךְ־פְּרִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֑יק אַ֥ךְ יֵשׁ־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים שֹׁפְטִ֥ים בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And will say humankind, Surely fruit [is] for the righteous; surely there is a God judging on the earth.
pieces: Then people will say, "Yes, the righteous do receive a reward; \q yes, a God does judge on the earth."

L.12: And humankind will say, "Surely [there is] fruit for the righteous; \q surely there is a God judging on the earth."

R.12: Then everyone will say, "It really does pay to do what is right. \q There really is a God who judges the world."

decisions.choice: fruit: reward, the result of a life
decisions.reason: Fruit is what a life produces and what it brings back to the one who lives it (1:3; Proverbs 1:31).

decisions.choice: a God judging: the true judge, unlike the false gods of verse 2
decisions.reason: The participle "judging" is plural, as Hebrew sometimes makes words agree with 'Elohim; the sense is the one God. The psalm ends where it began, with judging: the "gods" of verse 2 judged falsely, but God judges the earth.
